cards.title: Make a plan
cards.description: Hierophant: plan for a merge-ready change, not a draft
cards.prompt:
Create an implementation plan for the current task. Do not write code. No filler.

From context (if present): acceptance criteria; scope in / out; risks — data, interfaces, races, compatibility, regressions. Little context — at most 3 questions. Do not invent answers.

Rules: one step = one verifiable thing; per step — what to do · done criteria · how to verify; cover tests, errors, edges, rollback. Working simple beats ideal architecture. Assumptions — explicit. Do not invent interfaces, libraries, or commands that are not in the repo. If good open source exists — use it.

Output: numbered plan · risks · done criteria.
Next: «Evaluate the work».

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, and files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; people-pleasing; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: READY — plan is ready
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — more information needed

cards.title: Evaluate the work
cards.description: Justice: strict review with project quality score 0–10
cards.prompt:
Strict review of the current plan or change. Honestly, without flattery.

Project quality score 0–10: 0–6 block; 7–8 acceptable with caveats; 9–10 high bar. Do not accept below 7.
Check: correctness and edges; regressions; complexity; tests and errors; security and data if relevant; top-3 fixes for a merge request.
Do not inflate. For 9–10 you need 3 facts. If the goal is unclear or scope is bloated — do not score 7 or above.

Reply: score N/10 · verdict · critical / major / minor · fixes.
Large refactor only if asked.
Below 7 — «Tighten the plan». 7 or above — «Code it».

The project may be empty — judge only what exists.
Forbidden: inventing facts and gaps; inflating the score out of pity; scoring 9–10 without three facts; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

At the very end of the reply always add this line (N = your score 0-10):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If you cannot evaluate due to missing data, second line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA

cards.title: Tighten the plan
cards.description: Temperance: compress the plan to the minimum for implementation
cards.prompt:
Bring the plan to code-ready. Analysis only — no code.

Cut everything outside acceptance criteria. Clarify interfaces, data, errors, tests. If bloated — propose simpler with trade-offs. Keep steps and verification method. Do not invent requirements. Do not add “for later”.

Output: updated plan · change log (3–7 items) · plan readiness score 0–10.
7 or above — «Code it». Below 7 — tighten again.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing facts, names, numbers, and files; writing code (this card is analysis only); over-engineering “for later”; people-pleasing; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

At the very end of the reply always add this line (N = your score 0-10):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If you cannot evaluate due to missing data, second line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA

cards.title: Code it
cards.description: Magician: next step — verifiable code without regressions
cards.prompt:
Implement the next open step of the approved plan. Only this step.

Do not break what works. Handle errors explicitly. No data — 1–3 precise questions; do not invent interfaces or libraries. Before critical changes — backup. Do not add new features outside the step. Dangerous commands (delete, reset, production) — only after an explicit “yes”.

After: what changed · how to verify · risks. Goal — correctness score 7 or above.
Done — «Test it». Blocker — «Make a plan».

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing libraries, commands, and output; doing extras outside the step; people-pleasing and hiding breakage; dangerous commands without an explicit “yes”; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

End with one line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: DONE — step ready for verification
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: PARTIAL — step started but not finished
or
KEYCODE_STATUS: BLOCKED — need a human or data

cards.title: Test it
cards.description: Star: prove with a green run, not a promise
cards.prompt:
Verify what was just done as in continuous integration, not “should work”.

Commands, tests, build — with real output. Happy path + one edge case or failure (or why you cannot).
Red — cause and blocker; green — «TEST PASSED» and the checklist. Do not advance on red. If you cannot actually run checks — do not score above 4. If a human is needed — give a short scenario; do not mark «TEST PASSED». Do not fix code yourself unless asked.
Do not invent command output.
Result: green / red + project quality score 0–10 (below 7 = not ready).
7 or above — «Code it» (next step). Below 7 — «Fix bugs».

The project may be empty — judge only what exists.
Forbidden: inventing facts and gaps; inflating the score out of pity; scoring 9–10 without three facts; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

At the very end of the reply always add this line (N = your score 0-10):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If you cannot verify (no run or data), second line:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA

cards.title: Fix bugs
cards.description: Tower: minimal patch until score 7 or above
cards.prompt:
Fix the defect from the last test, review, or project quality score below 7 out of 10.

Minimal fix only. No drive-by refactors or new features. Before critical changes — backup.
Loop: symptom → cause → what else may break → patch → verify the same way. While score is below 7 — repeat.
After 3 attempts with no progress — stop: what fails and why; 2 options with trade-offs; list where a human is needed.
Format: was → became → evidence.
7 or above — «Test it».

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing libraries, commands, and output; doing extras outside the step; people-pleasing and hiding breakage; dangerous commands without an explicit “yes”; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

At the very end of the reply always add this line (N = your score 0-10):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If the step is not merely “scored”, second line one of:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — not enough data
KEYCODE_STATUS: BLOCKED — need a human or cannot go further

cards.title: Polish it
cards.description: Strength: raise project quality score to 9–10
cards.prompt:
High polish mode. Goal — project quality score 9 or 10. Stopping at 7–8 is not allowed.

Loop: score N/10 → critical and major gaps → fixes only for those (do not expand scope) → recheck → new score. While 8 or below — repeat.
Maximum 2–3 iterations. If the score does not rise for two rounds in a row — stop and explain the ceiling. If the ceiling is below 9 due to external limits — name them after exhausting in-scope fixes.
Before starting — backup.
Report: final score · what raised quality · residual risk · what you left alone.
9 or above — «Test it». «Do it all» — only if the whole scope is already closed.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing libraries, commands, and output; doing extras outside the step; people-pleasing and hiding breakage; dangerous commands without an explicit “yes”; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

At the very end of the reply always add this line (N = your score 0-10):
KEYCODE_SCORE: N
If the step is not merely “scored”, second line one of:
KEYCODE_STATUS: NEED_DATA — not enough data
KEYCODE_STATUS: BLOCKED — hit the ceiling, cannot go further

cards.title: Do it all
cards.description: World: end-to-end, each item score 7 or above
cards.prompt:
Full cycle through the plan. An item is closed only at score 7 or above (for 9–10 — «Polish it»). Per item: name → implement → verify with facts → score → fix until 7 → continue. No skipping, scope inflation, or masking red tests.
No plan — first 5–8 steps with acceptance criteria.
If the score does not rise for 2–3 rounds — simplify or change path. Need a human — list blockers, keep doing the rest. Three rounds with no movement — stop.
Before starting and on critical steps — backup. Dangerous commands — backup and explicit “yes”. Do not invent libraries or commands. If good open source exists — use it.
Finale: overall score · done / not done · risks · what to check manually before merge. Do not declare success below 7.

The project may be empty; it may have no rules. Do not invent what is not there.
Forbidden: inventing libraries, commands, and output; doing extras outside the step; people-pleasing and hiding breakage; dangerous commands without an explicit “yes”; if data is missing — ask, do not guess.

At the very end always:
KEYCODE_SCORE: N

If the approved scope is closed and checks are green:
KEYCODE_GATE: PASS
KEYCODE_NEXT: release-v1/release-plan

If not ready or checks are red:
KEYCODE_GATE: FAIL
If you stopped due to blockers:
KEYCODE_STATUS: BLOCKED

cards.title: Result overview
cards.description: High Priestess: briefly — task, done, gaps, next
cards.prompt:
Read this chat and the repo context. Do not write or change code. Do not invent evidence.

Four short blocks (1–3 items each):
1. Task — goal and acceptance criteria if known
2. Done
3. Not done — open items, failures, blockers
4. Next step — one card: Make a plan / Evaluate the work / Tighten the plan / Code it / Test it / Fix bugs / Polish it / Do it all

If there is no plan — recommend «Make a plan». If work stalled — fifth block: reason and options (simplify / return to plan / ask a human).
Do not add KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.

The project may be empty — write only what is visible in the chat.
Forbidden: inventing what was done; writing or changing code; adding KEYCODE_SCORE, KEYCODE_GATE, KEYCODE_NEXT, or KEYCODE_STATUS lines.
